Four panels labelled 'original', 'after translation', 'core critical points', 'lower X after translation' under a frameless nine-entry legend: solved is a solid blue contour, EFIT a dashed near-black one on one shared level array, the wall a grey polyline, and the six critical-point kinds are distinct glyphs. findings.summary: Solved and EFIT critical-point markers are each plotted at their own coordinate with no offset (draw_critical_points at line 200 for the solved census and line 201 for the EFIT one), so where the two fields agree the two glyphs overprint into a single mark the reader cannot decompose. On the 137 render this happens at four out-of-plasma points: solved maximum (R=1.0215, Z=+1.5291) over EFIT maximum (R=1.0228, Z=+1.5302), solved maximum (1.0303,-1.5351) over EFIT (1.0321,-1.5358), solved saddle (1.1090,-1.5617) over EFIT (1.1100,-1.5618) and solved saddle (1.1376,+1.5738) over EFIT (1.1357,+1.5723) -- pairwise separations of 1-3 mm, under half a pixel at the panel scale of about 238 px/m, which is why the marks at the top-left and bottom-left of both full-geometry panels read as one glyph rather than two. The 146 render shows the same at its own four coincident pairs. A reader cannot tell which of the six legend glyphs is on top, or that two points are drawn there. This does not hold the node: the affected points are exactly the ones the caption's closing clause labels as outside the main plasma, and the core and lower-X comparisons the figure exists for stay fully readable; a small leader or an inset count would recover the distinction if it is wanted.

Caption line 2 (render.py:257-263) states 'one physical contour-level array', but the core panel is drawn on an augmented array: line 144 takes the shared levels and adds six more at 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 mWb below the solved peak (line 147), so panel 3 does not share the level set the other three panels use. Within panel 3 the reference and solved fields do share that one augmented array, so the comparison inside the panel is fair; the defect is the caption's claim, which invites a reader to compare contour density between the 'after translation' panel and the core panel as if the two used one level set. Either the caption should say the core panel adds levels near the peak, or the panel should carry the shared array.

The four panels sit in equal-width grid columns while each poloidal panel keeps an equal aspect ratio, so the drawings fill only part of their column and the leftover becomes blank bands. Measured from the PNGs' own ink columns, the panels span 124-341 (217 px), 543-759 (216 px), 959-1172 (213 px) and 1297-1671 (374 px) on the 137 render, with blank gaps of 202, 200 and 125 px between them; the 146 render is the same apart from a 314 px core panel. The two full-geometry panels -- the side-by-side original against best translation that carries the comparison -- are thus the smallest on the canvas, and the fixed figure caption runs wider than any drawing above it. Nothing becomes unreadable, which is why this does not hold the node, and it is the same layout item the previous figure round raised; it is recorded again because it is still visible in this round's renders.
